post_text: Uku Joost Annus Raises €615K to Scale AI-Powered Mobile App Building. Estonian startup bilt.me has raised €614,900 ($700,000) in pre-seed funding to expand its AI-native platform that lets users turn an idea into a working mobile application. The round was led by Superhero Capital, with participation from Bolt founder Markus Villig and Lightyear founder Martin Sokk. Founded in August 2025, bilt.me began as a hackathon project in Tallinn before evolving into a platform focused specifically on native mobile applications. Its AI agent allows users to describe an app in plain language, generate a native iOS or Android application, preview it on a phone and work toward publishing on the App Store or Google Play. The early traction is notable: bilt.me says thousands of people are already building on the platform, while revenue has surpassed six figures in annual recurring revenue and doubled month over month for three consecutive months. The bigger shift: AI is moving from helping developers write code to taking users from an idea to a published mobile product.

We just ran the biggest hackathon Startup Garage has ever done! 85+ people. 36 teams. 18 mentors. 5 judges and an insane amount of vibe coded lines! Most of the participants had never written a line of code before Friday evening. By Saturday afternoon they had something built and were up showing it to mentors and the whole room. That was the whole point. We wanted to build a proper hackathon experience for people who'd never had one. Mentoring, workshops, a real expo round, a stage, pizza. The full thing, for high schoolers and first-year students who have never experienced a startup ecosystem event before. It worked. None of it happens without the people who backed us.

But personally I thought it was also the most boring thing I had ever heard in my life. So somehow I convinced them to make a tiktok brainrot app instead. People who have done this for years get great results with the exact same models. It's not the model. It's their prompts, their workflows, their taste. So we built Edge. The people who outperform you 10x package how they work as a skill, and your agent installs it. I spent a whole weekend building a video engine. post_text: Here's why honesty will take you far in the age of AI, fast outcomes, and big promises. I had a call today with a SaaS founder who wanted to start running ads (they are just starting out, no PMF). I asked him, 'Okay, can you tell me why people should choose your platform and who your ICP is?' Guess what... silence. Then I shared my approach to his product (messaging, positioning, and offer). He told me once again, 'But we have the budget; we just want some traffic.' I thought about it and said, 'If you need my help fixing your whole product, here's how I can help you, but anybody who would take your money to start running ads for you right now would be a thief.' He appreciated it and said it 'makes sense.' We didn't move forward. I could have easily closed this deal, but that's just not how I see our team.
